claims.text: Cellulitis is a clinical diagnosis: skin, wound and blood cultures are not routine.
claims.quote: Skin and wound cultures (including cutaneous aspirates, biopsies, or swabs) as well as blood cultures are not routinely recommended in all patients with cellulitis

claims.text: Blood cultures if immunocompromised or with systemic signs (fever, leukocytosis).
claims.quote: In patients who are immunocompromised and in patients who have signs of systemic infection (eg, fever and leukocytosis) (1), blood cultures may be useful for detecting bacteremia.

claims.text: Imaging for complications: point-of-care ultrasound for abscess, MRI for necrotizing soft-tissue infection.
claims.quote: Imaging modalities can effectively distinguish between cellulitis and abscess (eg, point of care ultrasound) or necrotizing soft-tissue infection (eg, MRI) and help guide management decisions

claims.text: Burns: map extent and depth; TBSA counts only partial- and full-thickness burns (rule of nines in adults, Lund-Browder chart in children).
claims.quote: The percentage of TBSA involved is calculated; only partial-thickness and full-thickness burns are included in this calculation (1). For adults, the percentage TBSA for parts of the body is estimated by the rule of nines and, for children, the Lund-Browder chart

claims.text: Burns > 20% TBSA in adults (> 15% in children): Hb/Hct, electrolytes, BUN, creatinine, albumin, protein, phosphate, ionized calcium, plus ECG, urinalysis for myoglobin and chest x-ray.
claims.quote: In hospitalized patients at risk for systemic complications (ie, adult patients with > 20% TBSA, children with > 15% TBSA, and older adult patients with electrical injuries with > 1K volt exposure and significant cardiac, pulmonary, or renal comorbidities), hemoglobin and hematocrit, serum electrolytes, blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, albumin, protein, phosphate, and ionized calcium should be measured. ECG, urinalysis for myoglobin, and a chest radiograph are also required.

claims.text: Suspected burn infection: confirm by biopsy; surface cultures are unreliable.
claims.quote: If the diagnosis is unclear, infection can be confirmed by biopsy; cultures from the wound surface or exudate are unreliable.
